This message is from Synchrony Bank, who wants to remind you to stay flexible.
Not the 10,000 steps before breakfast, yoga-bending, circus-performing, wish I hadn't done that kind of flexible.
It's about staying financially flexible, like with their high-yield savings account.
You'll earn a great rate without monthly fees or minimums that can slow your progress.
Go to Synchrony.com/NPR. Remember FDIC.
There were reporters were blocked from covering President Trump's state dinner with Chinese President Xi Jinping at the White House.
That comes after journalists from those outlets in Politico returned to the White House today,
following a federal judge's order for Trump to restore their access.
NPR's Brian Mann reports on the president's response to the ruling.
Writing on his truth social platform, Trump again accused U.S. journalists without offering evidence of conspiring to make up false stories about him.
Then, according to a pool report from press photographers with Trump today during his meeting with Xi,
Trump reportedly made a joke about China having the friendliest press corps.
China, of course, is a communist nation with overwhelming government control over free speech and the press.
NPR's Brian Mann reporting.
New York City police arrested more than 100 people outside the U.N. headquarters today,
as Walter Wuthman of WNYC reports, activists protested Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's speech to the General Assembly.
Hundreds of protesters shut down traffic at a major intersection near the U.N. headquarters.
Dozens then refused police orders to leave the area, including Daria Lisa of Vila Chevalier,
a Democratic socialist in the nominee for an upper Manhattan congressional seat.
Somebody, if it won't be our presidential administration or other elected officials, needs to know that accountability must happen,
that you cannot enact a genocide and walk freely through the streets of New York.
The Israeli leader used his speech to dismiss accusations of genocide.
Many of those arrested are political allies of Mayor Zoran Mamdani, whom Netanyahu frequently criticized in that speech.
For NPR News, I'm Walter Wuthman in New York.
African leaders at the U.N. General Assembly are demanding reform at the Security Council to include permanent seats for African countries.
Many African heads of state have expressed frustration over the continent's lack of permanent representation as they navigate global security issues.
A grand jury has issued no indictments in the case of Nolan Wells, the teenager found dead off of the Mississippi coast in July.
Attorneys for the family are sharing their findings, though, as questions remain.
Elise Gregg of the Gulf States newsroom has more on findings from Wells' cell phone.
Forensic investigator Andrew Garrett at a press conference in Orlando talked through findings from the cell phone extraction.
Things were deleted on the phone from the time he last had the phone up until the time that his parents got the phone.
Garrett and his team have been working with attorney Ben Crump in his office.
They comb through phone data, including Snapchat messages and group conversations.
And what they eventually found appears to contradict earlier statements by the Jackson County prosecutor who said a preliminary report indicated no messages were deleted since Wells' last use.
For NPR News, I'm Elise Gregg in Jackson, Mississippi.
U.S. stock indexes ended roughly back where they started today after an up and down day.
The S&P 500 was virtually unchanged.
This is NPR News.
Major Chinese auto group Geely has unveiled new charging technology that can recharge an electric vehicle battery from 10 percent to 70 percent in just four and a half minutes.
It's an attempt to narrow the gap with the conventional five minute gas refueling time.
Chinese cars are effectively banned in the U.S.
When President Trump took office, he vowed to dismantle the Education Department, saying that changes wouldn't affect sending money to America's neediest students.
But as NPR's Janaki Mehta reports, federal education employees tell a different story.
NPR spoke to five current employees at the agency who all asked not to be named because they fear losing their jobs.
The Education Department told NPR the changes will increase efficiency.
But workers say being scattered across several federal agencies makes sending money to states and schools less efficient, partly because staffers used to manage grants with one system at education.
Now some are using several systems at other agencies they say aren't built for education grants.
NPR also found moving people in and out of the department may be costing taxpayer dollars.
Ed workers are moving out of a building that was just renovated for their needs.
It may cost hundreds of millions more to update the building again for the energy department, which is supposed to move in.
Janaki Mehta, NPR News. Scientists at Stanford University have discovered that the brain may consist of two separate organs that evolved independently.
One system controls vital functions like breathing, while the other handles higher level operations like language and consciousness.
The discovery could advance research into conditions like ALS.
I'm Ryland Barton. This is NPR News from Washington.
This message is from Synchrony Bank, who can help you get your do nothing savings to work hard with their high yield savings account.
Put your lazy savings to work at Synchrony.com/NPR.
Member FDIC.
